name: Zeus
title: Greek deity mentioned in Acts of the Apostles
lifespan: Not a biblical person – Greek deity
summary: Zeus is the supreme god in Greek mythology and is mentioned in the Bible in connection with Paul's missionary journeys. In Lystra, the inhabitants tried to worship Paul and Barnabas as Zeus and Hermes after they performed a miracle. Zeus is not a biblical figure but is referred to as an idol in contrast to the living God.

keyEvents.title: The crowd in Lystra calls Barnabas Zeus
keyEvents.description: After Paul healed a lame man in Lystra, the crowd believed that gods had come down to them in human form. They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes.

keyEvents.title: Priest of Zeus brings sacrificial animals
keyEvents.description: The priest from the temple of Zeus outside the city brought oxen and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas along with the crowd.

keyEvents.title: Paul and Barnabas reject idol worship
keyEvents.description: Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes, ran out among the people, and shouted that they were mere men, urging them to turn away from these empty idols to the living God.

keyEvents.title: Altar of Zeus in Athens
keyEvents.description: When Paul was in Athens, he noticed that the city was full of idols, including worship of Greek gods like Zeus. He spoke at the Areopagus about the unknown God in contrast to the idols.

keyEvents.title: Reference to Zeus in the Letter to Titus
keyEvents.description: Paul quotes the Cretan poet Epimenides, who originally wrote about Zeus, when he says 'For in him we live and move and have our being', using the quote in a new context about the true God.
